facts.statement: The genus name Wannanosaurus means "Wannan lizard" and refers to the place where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: Wannanosaurus (meaning "Wannan lizard", named after the location where it was discovered)

facts.statement: The species Wannanosaurus yansiensis was described by Hou Lian-Hai in 1977.
facts.quote: The type species Wannanosaurus yansiensis was described by Hou Lian-Hai in 1977.

facts.statement: The animal is known from a single partial skeleton consisting of a partial skull roof, lower jaw, femur, tibia, rib fragments, and other pieces.
facts.quote: It is known from a single partial skeleton, including a partial skull roof and lower jaw, a femur and tibia, part of a rib, and other fragments.

facts.statement: Its flat skull roof with large openings suggests it was a primitive member of the pachycephalosaur group.
facts.quote: Because it has a flat skull roof with large openings, it has been considered primitive among pachycephalosaurs.

facts.statement: Wannanosaurus was sometimes classified in the now-deprecated family Homalocephalidae, which grouped pachycephalosaurs lacking domed skulls.
facts.quote: Sometimes it has been classified as a member of the now-deprecated family Homalocephalidae, now thought to be an unnatural assembly of pachycephalosaurs without domed skulls.

facts.statement: The known specimen had a femur about 8 cm long and an estimated total length of 60 cm, yet fused skull bones indicate it was an adult when it died.
facts.quote: Although its remains are from a very small individual, with a femur length of approximately 8 cm and an estimated overall length of about 60 cm, the fused bones in its skull suggest that it was an adult at death.

facts.statement: Wannanosaurus was likely a herbivore or omnivore that fed close to the ground on plants and possibly insects.
facts.quote: Like other pachycephalosaurs, it was probably herbivorous or omnivorous, feeding close to the ground on a variety of plant matter, and possibly insects as well.

facts.statement: Wannanosaurus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 69 million years ago in the Maastrichtian, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 72 a 69 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Wannanosaurus were found in red sandstone sediments of the Xiaoyan Formation in Anhui, China.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles fueron encontrados en sedimentos de arenisca roja de la Formación Xiaoyan, en Anhui, China.

facts.statement: With a femur measuring only 8 centimeters, the known specimen was estimated to be about 60 centimeters long and was an adult at death due to fused cranial sutures.
facts.quote: Debido a lo pequeño de los restos, el fémur solo medía 8 centímetros, se piensa que no alcanzaba al metro de largo, estimando que el ejemplar conocido apenas llegaba a los 60 centímetros, que debido a la fusión de las suturas craneales era un adulto al morir.

facts.statement: A cladogram based on analyses by Butler and colleagues from 2011 shows the classification of Wannanosaurus.
facts.quote: A continuación vemos un cladograma según los analísi de Butler y colaboradores de 2011.

facts.statement: The time range for Wannanosaurus is the Maastrichtian, spanning from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
